_meta.note: Full name (acronyms expanded) + 1-2 sentence clinical description per marker, keyed by the exact marker name string in pillars.json. Drives the rich hover on the Pillar weights & correlations diagram. Authored from standard clinical definitions; illustrative, re-verify (README §5.6).

Systolic BP.desc: The peak arterial pressure during ventricular contraction; a leading driver of cardiovascular, cerebrovascular, and kidney disease risk.

Diastolic BP.desc: The arterial pressure between heartbeats while the heart relaxes and fills; elevations raise cardiovascular and stroke risk, especially in younger adults.

ApoB.desc: Counts all atherogenic lipoprotein particles (each carries one ApoB); the most direct measure of particle number driving atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease risk.

LDL-C.desc: Cholesterol carried by LDL particles that deposits in artery walls; a primary causal driver of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease and a key treatment target.

HDL-C.desc: Cholesterol carried by HDL particles involved in reverse cholesterol transport; low levels mark elevated cardiovascular risk, though it is a risk marker, not a target.

Lp(a).desc: A genetically determined LDL-like particle bound to apolipoprotein(a); elevated levels independently raise risk of atherosclerosis, heart attack, and aortic stenosis.

Resting HR.desc: Heartbeats per minute at rest; an indicator of cardiovascular fitness and autonomic tone, with higher rates linked to greater cardiovascular and all-cause mortality risk.

HRV (RMSSD, age-adj).full: Heart Rate Variability (Root Mean Square of Successive Differences, age-adjusted)
HRV (RMSSD, age-adj).desc: Beat-to-beat variation reflecting parasympathetic (vagal) autonomic activity; lower age-adjusted values signal stress, poor recovery, and higher cardiovascular risk.

CAC.desc: A CT-derived score quantifying calcified plaque in the coronary arteries; directly measures subclinical atherosclerosis and strongly predicts future cardiac events.

HbA1c.desc: Reflects average blood glucose over the prior ~3 months via glucose bound to hemoglobin; used to diagnose and monitor diabetes and gauge metabolic risk.

Fasting glucose.desc: Blood glucose after an overnight fast; screens for and diagnoses impaired glucose regulation and diabetes, reflecting baseline glycemic control.

Fasting insulin.desc: Circulating insulin after an overnight fast; elevated levels signal insulin resistance and compensatory hyperinsulinemia, an early marker of metabolic dysfunction.

HOMA-IR.full: Homeostatic Model Assessment of Insulin Resistance
HOMA-IR.desc: A calculated index from fasting glucose and insulin estimating insulin resistance; higher values indicate worse insulin sensitivity and metabolic syndrome risk.

Triglycerides.desc: Fat carried in the blood by lipoproteins; elevated levels reflect metabolic dysfunction and insulin resistance and contribute to atherosclerotic cardiovascular risk.

Waist circumference.desc: A measure of central (visceral) abdominal adiposity; higher values indicate greater metabolic syndrome, insulin resistance, and cardiovascular risk independent of weight.

CGM time-in-range.desc: The percentage of time glucose stays within a target range (typically 70-180 mg/dL); a higher value reflects better day-to-day glycemic control and lower complication risk.

CGM glycemic variability.desc: The degree of fluctuation in glucose over time (e.g., coefficient of variation); higher variability indicates unstable control and added metabolic and cardiovascular risk.

eGFR (cystatin-C).desc: An estimate of kidney filtering capacity derived from serum cystatin C; less affected by muscle mass than creatinine, it refines staging and risk in chronic kidney disease.

eGFR (creatinine).desc: An estimate of kidney filtering capacity from serum creatinine; the primary marker for diagnosing and staging chronic kidney disease.

UACR.desc: Measures albumin leakage into urine relative to creatinine; an early marker of kidney damage and a strong predictor of renal and cardiovascular risk.

Potassium.desc: The main intracellular electrolyte regulating nerve and muscle function; abnormal levels disturb cardiac rhythm and often reflect kidney or hormonal dysfunction.

Sodium.desc: The main extracellular electrolyte governing fluid balance and osmolality; abnormal levels signal water imbalance and affect neurological and cardiovascular function.

ALT.desc: A liver-specific enzyme released into blood when hepatocytes are injured; a core marker of liver-cell damage and metabolic liver disease.

AST.desc: An enzyme from liver, muscle, and heart released on tissue injury; elevated levels indicate hepatocellular damage, especially when interpreted alongside ALT.

GGT.desc: A biliary enzyme that rises with bile-duct obstruction, alcohol use, and oxidative stress; helps confirm hepatic origin of enzyme elevations.

FIB-4 index.desc: A calculated score from age, AST, ALT, and platelets that estimates the likelihood of advanced liver fibrosis, used to triage who needs further evaluation.

Liver fat (CAP / MRI-PDFF).full: Liver Fat (Controlled Attenuation Parameter / Magnetic Resonance Imaging Proton Density Fat Fraction)
Liver fat (CAP / MRI-PDFF).desc: Quantifies fat accumulation in the liver by ultrasound or MRI; the defining measure of steatotic (fatty) liver disease and metabolic risk.

Bilirubin.desc: A heme breakdown product cleared by the liver; elevated levels cause jaundice and signal impaired liver function, bile-flow obstruction, or excess red-cell breakdown.

hsCRP.desc: An acute-phase protein measured at low concentrations to gauge low-grade systemic inflammation; a marker of cardiovascular and metabolic risk.

WBC.desc: The total count of circulating immune cells; elevations suggest infection or inflammation while low counts indicate impaired immunity or marrow suppression.

Ferritin (as inflammation).desc: Beyond reflecting iron stores, ferritin rises as a positive acute-phase reactant during inflammation, making elevated levels a nonspecific inflammatory signal.

Neutrophil:Lymphocyte ratio.desc: The ratio of neutrophils to lymphocytes in blood; a simple index of systemic inflammation and physiologic stress that predicts adverse outcomes across many diseases.

IL-6.desc: A pro-inflammatory cytokine that drives the acute-phase response; elevated levels mark active inflammation and predict cardiovascular and metabolic risk.

Albumin (inverse APR).desc: The main blood protein that falls during inflammation as a negative acute-phase reactant; low levels reflect inflammation, poor nutrition, or liver and kidney loss.

Skin temp deviation.desc: The departure of skin temperature from an individual's baseline, often from wearables; shifts can signal infection, inflammation, or circadian and hormonal changes.

Hemoglobin.desc: The iron-containing protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen from the lungs to tissues; low levels define anemia, causing fatigue and reduced oxygen delivery.

Hematocrit.desc: The percentage of blood volume occupied by red blood cells; low values indicate anemia or blood loss, while high values suggest dehydration or polycythemia.

RDW.desc: The variability in red blood cell size; elevated values flag anemias and independently predict cardiovascular and all-cause mortality.

Platelets.desc: Cell fragments essential for blood clotting; low counts raise bleeding risk while high counts can promote clotting, and both flag marrow, immune, or inflammatory disorders.

Iron saturation.desc: The percentage of transferrin's iron-binding sites occupied by iron; low values indicate iron deficiency, while high values suggest iron overload such as hemochromatosis.

SpO₂.desc: The percentage of hemoglobin saturated with oxygen, measured non-invasively by pulse oximetry; low values signal hypoxemia from respiratory or circulatory compromise.

Ferritin (iron stores).desc: The intracellular protein storing iron; the primary marker of body iron stores, with low levels confirming iron deficiency and high levels indicating overload or inflammation.

TSH.desc: A pituitary hormone driving thyroid hormone production; the most sensitive screen for thyroid function, with high levels indicating hypothyroidism and low levels hyperthyroidism.

Free T4.desc: The unbound, biologically active form of the thyroid hormone thyroxine; reflects true thyroid output and helps confirm and grade hypo- or hyperthyroidism alongside TSH.

Cortisol rhythm (diurnal slope).desc: The decline in cortisol from its morning peak to evening trough; a flattened slope reflects HPA-axis dysregulation and is linked to chronic stress and poorer health outcomes.

Sex hormones (E2/Prog/FSH/LH/T/SHBG/AMH).full: Oestradiol, Progesterone, Follicle-Stimulating Hormone, Luteinising Hormone, Testosterone, Sex-Hormone-Binding Globulin, Anti-Müllerian Hormone
Sex hormones (E2/Prog/FSH/LH/T/SHBG/AMH).desc: A reproductive-endocrine panel assessing gonadal and pituitary function, fertility, ovarian reserve (AMH), and bioavailable hormone levels (SHBG) across the sexes.

Fasting cortisol.desc: Cortisol measured in the fasting morning state near its diurnal peak; screens for adrenal insufficiency when low and Cushing's syndrome or stress when high.

Prolactin.desc: A pituitary hormone driving lactation; elevated levels can disrupt menstruation, fertility, and libido and may signal a pituitary adenoma or medication effect.

BMI.desc: Weight in kilograms divided by height in metres squared (kg/m²); a quick screening proxy for under- or over-weight, though it cannot distinguish fat from muscle.

Body fat % (DEXA).full: Body Fat Percentage by Dual-Energy X-ray Absorptiometry
Body fat % (DEXA).desc: Proportion of total body mass that is fat tissue, measured precisely by DEXA; a key indicator of adiposity and metabolic and cardiovascular risk.

ALMI / lean mass index.desc: Arm and leg lean (muscle) mass from DEXA normalised to height squared (kg/m²); the core measure for diagnosing sarcopenia and frailty risk.

Grip strength.desc: Maximal force generated by squeezing a dynamometer; a validated marker of overall muscle strength that predicts frailty, disability and all-cause mortality.

Gait speed.desc: Time taken to walk a short set distance, expressed in metres per second; a powerful predictor of mobility, frailty, falls and survival in ageing adults.

BMD T-score (DEXA).full: Bone Mineral Density T-score by Dual-Energy X-ray Absorptiometry
BMD T-score (DEXA).desc: Bone density expressed as standard deviations from a healthy young-adult mean; defines osteopenia and osteoporosis and predicts fracture risk.

Visceral adipose.desc: Fat stored deep in the abdomen around internal organs; metabolically active and strongly linked to insulin resistance, type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular disease.

25-OH Vitamin D.desc: The main circulating form of vitamin D and the standard marker of vitamin D status; essential for calcium absorption, bone health and immune function.

Vitamin B12.desc: A B-vitamin needed for red blood cell formation, DNA synthesis and nerve function; deficiency causes megaloblastic anaemia and neurological damage.

Folate.desc: A B-vitamin essential for DNA synthesis and red blood cell production; deficiency causes megaloblastic anaemia and raises neural-tube-defect risk in pregnancy.

Ferritin (stores).desc: The iron-storage protein whose blood level reflects total body iron reserves; low values indicate iron deficiency, while high values can signal inflammation or overload.

Omega-3 index.desc: Percentage of EPA plus DHA omega-3 fatty acids in red blood cell membranes; a marker of long-term omega-3 status linked to lower cardiovascular risk.

Magnesium.desc: An essential mineral and cofactor for hundreds of enzymes involved in energy, muscle and nerve function; deficiency can cause cramps, arrhythmias and weakness.

Diet-quality (HEI/Mediterranean).full: Diet Quality (Healthy Eating Index / Mediterranean Diet Score)
Diet-quality (HEI/Mediterranean).desc: Scores measuring how closely eating patterns align with healthy dietary guidelines; higher scores predict lower chronic-disease and mortality risk.

Fiber intake.desc: Daily intake of indigestible plant carbohydrate; supports gut health, glycaemic control and cholesterol, and higher intake lowers cardiovascular and bowel-cancer risk.

Sleep duration (14-day mean).desc: Average total nightly sleep time over 14 days from a wearable; chronic short (<7h) or long (>9h) sleep is linked to cardiometabolic, cognitive, and mortality risk.

Sleep regularity index.desc: A 0–100 metric of day-to-day consistency in sleep–wake timing; lower regularity, independent of duration, predicts cardiometabolic and mortality risk.

Sleep efficiency.desc: Percentage of time in bed actually spent asleep; values below ~85% indicate fragmented or disrupted sleep and reduced restorative quality.

Deep + REM proportion.desc: Share of sleep in deep slow-wave and rapid-eye-movement stages; these stages drive physical recovery, memory consolidation, and emotional regulation.

Overnight SpO₂ / ODI (apnea).full: Overnight Oxygen Saturation / Oxygen Desaturation Index (sleep apnea)
Overnight SpO₂ / ODI (apnea).desc: Tracks blood-oxygen saturation overnight; the Oxygen Desaturation Index counts desaturations per hour as a marker of sleep apnea and nocturnal hypoxemia.

Nighttime HR/HRV recovery.full: Nighttime Heart Rate / Heart Rate Variability Recovery
Nighttime HR/HRV recovery.desc: Resting overnight heart rate and heart-rate variability reflecting parasympathetic recovery; higher HRV and lower resting HR indicate better autonomic and cardiovascular health.

VO₂max (est.).desc: Wearable-estimated peak rate of oxygen consumption during exercise; a leading index of cardiorespiratory fitness and a strong predictor of all-cause mortality.

MVPA.desc: Time spent in moderate-to-vigorous-intensity activity; meeting ~150 min/week lowers cardiovascular, metabolic, and mortality risk.

Steps/day (14-day mean).desc: Average daily step count over 14 days as a measure of overall physical activity; higher counts (up to ~7,000–10,000) are associated with reduced mortality.

Sedentary time.desc: Daily time spent in low-energy sitting or reclining; prolonged sedentary behavior independently raises cardiometabolic and mortality risk even in active people.

Grip strength (shared w/ BCM).full: Handgrip Strength (shared with Body Composition & Musculoskeletal)
Grip strength (shared w/ BCM).desc: Maximal hand-grip force as a proxy for whole-body muscle strength; low grip strength predicts frailty, sarcopenia, disability, and mortality.

HR recovery (wearable).desc: Drop in heart rate in the first minute(s) after exercise; faster recovery reflects healthy parasympathetic reactivation and lower cardiovascular risk.

PHQ-9 (depression).desc: A 9-item self-report screen for depression severity; scores 0–27 stratify none/mild/moderate/severe and item 9 screens suicidality.

GAD-7 (anxiety).desc: A 7-item self-report scale for anxiety severity; scores 0–21 stratify minimal/mild/moderate/severe generalized anxiety.

Perceived stress (PSS).desc: A self-report scale measuring how unpredictable and overloaded one perceives life to be; higher scores correlate with poorer mental and physical health outcomes.

Loneliness (UCLA-3).desc: A brief 3-item measure of subjective loneliness and social isolation; higher scores are linked to elevated cardiovascular, cognitive, and mortality risk.

Cognitive screen (age-adj).desc: A brief age-adjusted assessment of cognitive function (memory, attention, executive function) to detect impairment relative to age-expected norms.

Subjective wellbeing (WHO-5).desc: A 5-item self-report of positive mood and vitality over two weeks; scores 0–100 gauge psychological wellbeing, with ≤50 flagging possible low mood or depression.
